commit.message:
Studio: restore right-click menus in empty media panes (#141)

## What and why

Right-clicking an empty media library or folder did not open its context
menu: the full-size empty-state element received the event, while the
handler only accepted clicks directly on the scroll container. Users had
to add an item before they could reach **Link files…** or **Link a
folder…** from the background.

Handle background context menus on the scroll container, including
events from empty-state text/icons, search-empty messages and list
headers. Keep file/folder actions and editable controls separate, and
remove the redundant grid handler.

Includes an isolated Electron regression covering empty and populated
panes, file/folder picker entry points, folder naming, item menus,
search results and Saved's existing action restrictions. The pickers are
cancelled; the test never touches personal media.

## Validation

- Passed `pnpm typecheck` for every workspace.
- Passed `node apps/desktop/bench/media-menu.test.mjs` on Windows with
Node 22.23.3. The empty-background case fails before the fix.
- Passed the public audit and Gitleaks 8.30.1 against a clean export of
the exact committed sources.
- [Three-platform CI, packaging and
audit](https://github.com/WeiXunWuMing/openfilm/actions/runs/39394692284)
**all passed** on commit `398671cf56811c9f8fe73154b425533ce87af7b0`,
using the repository's unmodified `ci.yml`. Every platform passed type
checks and the complete workspace test command:

| Platform | Passed | Failed | Existing platform/environment skips |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Linux | 1,412 | 0 | 7 |
| macOS | 1,414 | 0 | 5 |
| Windows | 1,399 | 0 | 20 |

The skips are existing checks whose platform prerequisites are
unavailable; no tests or assertions were disabled for this fix. The
[upstream CI
run](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/actions/runs/39394780489)
currently awaits maintainer approval (`action_required`); the successful
fork run above tested the same PR commit.

Only the fix, regression test, test command documentation and patch
changeset are included. No dependencies, installer binaries or local
account data are included.

## Checklist

- [x] One change
- [x] A regression test for the bug
- [x] SPEC.md: not applicable; no film format changes
- [x] New media provider requirements: not applicable
- [x] `pnpm test` and `pnpm typecheck` pass on all three CI platforms

commit.message:
Add Gemini audio transcription (#132)

## What and why

Adds Gemini audio transcription to the existing Google provider,
allowing people to generate captions with their own Gemini API key.
Audio is transcribed with word-level timestamps and the temporary Gemini
upload is deleted afterward.

## Real service run

Run against Google Gemini with a connected personal API key (the key is
not shown):

```console
$ openfilm get asr --src assets/audio/gemini-check.wav --via google --model gemini-3.5-transcribe --force
{
  "src": "assets/audio/gemini-check.wav",
  "text": "Open film Gemini transcription works on this real audio sample.",
  "transcript": "assets/audio/gemini-check.vtt"
}
```

The generated WebVTT contained word-level timestamps from `00:00:00.100`
through `00:00:03.700`. The source was a 3.99-second synthetic WAV
saying: “OpenFilm Gemini transcription works on this real audio sample.”
The uploaded Gemini file was deleted after transcription.

This extends the existing Google provider, so its mark and translated
provider words are unchanged.

- [x] One change

- [x] SPEC.md updated, if it changes film.html
- [x] A new media provider: tests against a fake service, what the real
service did (never a key), its mark, its words in five languages
- [x] `pnpm test` and `pnpm typecheck` pass

Skills installed and kept on or off, projects and tabs in step, playback settings and component properties (#145)

## What and why

The changes tested locally since 0.2.2, together for the next release.

**Skills**
- Installed: yours first, then the OpenFilm skills you installed, this
project's, and each agent's own (off until you turn one on). Each has a
switch: on, an agent takes it up whenever it fits; off, no agent gets
it.
- Discover: OpenFilm's official skills as a catalog. One is installed to
be used.
- A skill opens as its page (picture left, words right) with its switch,
Install or Try now (a new conversation with the skill named), and
Uninstall or Move to trash.
- Agents' sessions, the message box's list and `openfilm skills` get
only skills installed and on. Kept in the shared prefs.json, so every
OpenFilm on the computer agrees.
- A skill named in a message is for that message. Its SKILL.md goes to
the agent once per conversation, unseen in the chat. The earlier "keep
on in this project" is gone.

**Projects and tabs**
- Deleting, renaming or moving a project keeps every tab in step; a
deleted project's tabs close together; going back never hangs on a
project that is gone.
- Moving shows the folders as a tree, and folders themselves can be
moved.
- New project opens in one click without a flash.

**Studio**
- Playback settings in the viewer replace the loop button; the canvas
shape is the inspector's.
- Component properties for page clips; a picture inside a page is
replaced on the picture; a page in Saved plays.
- Sound at another speed keeps its pitch in the preview.
- Export is an icon again; a chosen project's outline shows whole.

**CI**
- The nightly agent check puts node on the macOS login shell's PATH,
where npm's global agents are (#142 failed on that, not on the app).
